name: Christmas skins picture workflow B: Snowflake Nutmeg, First Snow Cloud, Sugar Plum Holly, Nutcracker Clone and Carol Singer Harmony
picture_standard: This is a Christmas outfit for a character in a kids' co-op escape game for ages 8 and up: festive, cozy and fun, never scary. For a FRONT view the attached picture is this SAME character's approved look: keep the face, skin tone, eyes, hair, body shape and proportions exactly the same, with a friendly happy expression - change ONLY the clothes and accessories as described. For a BACK view the attached picture is the new outfit from the front: show the same character from directly behind, same pose, every color the same as the front. Clean, simple 3D cartoon toy style exactly like the attached picture: every area one smooth, flat, solid color, with no texture at all - no fabric grain, no knit, no fluffy fur strands, no stitching, no sparkles or glitter, no folds or wrinkles painted on, no shading or shadows painted on, nothing see-through and nothing glowing (lights are solid bright colors). Small details as simple solid shapes, close to the body - nothing thin or long sticking out (no strings, no straps hanging loose, no scarf ends flying). No logos, brand marks, emblems, swooshes, stripes on shoes, printed words, letters, numbers or graphics. Not like any famous character from a film, cartoon, ballet production or game. Full body standing in an A-pose: arms straight and angled clearly down and away from the body with a clear gap between each arm and the body all the way down, hands open, legs slightly apart, feet flat. Centered and filling the whole height, nothing cropped. Plain flat light-gray background, even soft light, no floor shadow. One character only, no text.
instructions: Process all ten assets strictly in table order. Include the complete picture_standard verbatim, two newlines, then the row picture verbatim in every prompt.
Resolve references beneath reference_root; inspect and attach only the listed reference for each row.
Save and verify each FRONT at its file_name before generating the next BACK; attach that newly saved FRONT as the BACK reference.
Create missing output folders; preserve existing artwork unless replacement is explicitly requested.
Inspect likeness, full-body A-pose, arm gaps, outfit details, colors, smooth surfaces, background, no text/logos, and front/back consistency.
Record generated source, saved path, dimensions, SHA-256 and visual validation for each image.
